title: Manager transition: 90-day ramp, hiring priorities and onboarding checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for transitioning new engineering managers into their first 90 days while running a compact hiring plan for the serving/runtime org. Goal is to give a repeatable, low-friction ramp + hiring template that balances team stability, few high-impact hires, and handoff hygiene.

Context / scope:
- Audience: people-ops, hiring managers, onboarding buddy, recruiting partner.
- Target role for this doc: new EMs in infra-serving/runtime or adjacent infra teams that ship inference serving.
- Style: pragmatic checklist and lightweight interview rubric; intentionally opinionated to shorten hiring cycles.

Top-level outcomes (90 days):
1) Team clarity: documented charter + top 3 priorities owned by manager and shared with team.
2) Hiring progress: 2 identified priority hires in interviewing funnel; 1 offer extended if baseline headcount available.
3) Operational handoff: ownership of on-call rotations, runbooks, and CI/CD rollouts transferred and validated.
4) Onboarding completion: 1:1s with all direct reports finished; first sprint planning led by manager.

Hiring priorities (mini-plan):
- Week 0: Align with Eng + Product on top 3 gaps (latency, reliability, cost). Confirm hiring band + approval.
- Priority slots (example): 1x Senior Backend (models infra), 1x Staff Site Reliability (serving reliability), 1x SWE (optional, backlog-driven).
- Sourcing channels: internal referrals first, targeted outreach from recruiting, and 1 hire-from-contractor pipeline.
- Interview velocity target: screen -> ons -> decision within 21 calendar days for strong IC candidates.

Interview rubric (compact, 4 buckets, 0–3 scoring):
Scoring legend: 0 = no signal / red flag, 1 = partial skill, 2 = solid, 3 = exceptional.
- Technical depth (system design / architecture): evaluates ability to design low-latency serving systems, capacity planning, tradeoffs.
- Production judgment (reliability & ops): incident triage, monitoring choices, runbook authorship, SLO tradeoffs.
- Execution & collaboration (delivery): estimates, cross-team communication, PR review quality.
- Leadership & craft (for senior/staff / or IC leadership): mentorship, design reviews, roadmap influence.

Role-specific emphasis:
- Senior Backend: heavy weight on Technical depth (40%), Production judgment (30%), Execution (20%), Leadership (10%).
- Staff SRE: Production judgment (40%), Technical depth (25%), Execution (20%), Leadership (15%).

Sample screen questions (phone / 45m):
- "Walk me through a recent incident where latency spiked in production — how did you investigate and what mitigations did you implement?" (probe: metrics, KV cache, batching effects)
- "Design a simple inference service that supports streaming responses and can autoscale to 10k req/s. What are the tradeoffs?"
- "Tell me about a time you pushed back on a roadmap decision for technical debt — outcome and reasoning."

Onsite / take-home focus areas:
- Small architecture whiteboard: end-to-end inference request flow, cache management, tokenization boundary issues.
- Pragmatic debugging exercise: given traces/metrics, find bottleneck and propose 2 prioritized remediations.
- Optional take-home: small code exercise to show idiomatic telemetry or retry logic.

Candidate experience expectations:
- Clear timeline provided at screen stage; recruiter to confirm interview loop within 48 hours.
- Candidate feedback collected in 48 hours after onsite.
- Recruiter + hiring manager to own offer cadence.

Onboarding checklist (first 30 / 60 / 90):
Day 0–7 (getting set up):
- Access: workspace, corporate VPN, KMS access request submitted and validated.
- Tools: GitHub, Linear, Datadog, Napa dashboard, CI/CD perms verified.
- Intro meetings scheduled: direct reports, product PM, infra partner, on-call buddy assigned.
- Review: team charter, current roadmap, most recent incidents, cost dashboard.

Week 2–4 (context & first wins):
- Run first 1:1s cadence (30–45m) with all directs, capture key signals: blockers, morale, onboarding blockers.
- Shadow on-call rotation once; review primary runbooks and postmortem backlog.
- Deliverable: draft of top-3 priorities and a 30/60/90 public doc shared with exec.

Month 2 (stabilize and hire):
- Take ownership of one operational dashboard and shipping cadence.
- Start running interview loop; aim to progress 2–3 candidates/week.
- Schedule hiring calibration with Eng leads and recruiting.

Month 3 (scale & handoff):
- Validate that runbooks are up-to-date and run a tabletop for a common incident.
- Complete at least 2 hiring debriefs and extend an offer if aligned.
- Handoff note: create a 1-page team-state summary for next manager check-in.

Handoff template (what outgoing manager should leave):
- Team roster with strengths/areas for growth (one line per person).
- Active projects, owners, status, and known risks.
- On-call schedule, escalation paths, and top 3 recurring incidents.
- Open hiring pipeline links (screens/ons/offer lanes) and outstanding approvals.

Meet cadence (recommended first 90):
- Weekly skip-level with exec (30m) — first meeting week 2.
- Weekly 1:1s with directs.
- Biweekly hiring sync with recruiter + people-ops.
- Monthly roadmap review with Product.

Success metrics (90d signals):
- Team clarity: >80% of team can articulate top-3 priorities in a quick survey.
- Hiring velocity: at least 2 candidates in ons or 1 offer extended.
- Operational maturity: mean time to acknowledge alerts decreased by 20% on a chosen SLO.

Open questions / risk items (notes to self):
- Headcount approval timeline unclear for Q4 — recruiting to escalate if not approved by EOW.
- Dependency on a single CD pipeline; if broken, hiring timeline slips.
- Need to confirm budget bands for contractor convert to perm.

Quick links (internal):
- Serving runtime roadmap (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/Serving+Runtime+Roadmap
- Oncall runbooks folder: GDrive:/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/oncall-runbooks
- Interview scorecard template: GDrive:/shared_drives/people-ops/interview-templates/compact-scorecard.md

Notes to people-ops / recruiting partners:
- Prioritize referrals and contractor conversions for speed.
- Use compact 3-interviewer loop to reduce candidate dropoff.
- Provide hiring manager with a template email for offers and counteroffers (I can draft).

Last thoughts (working):
- This doc is intentionally short and actionable. Will iterate after first EM transition: capture lessons (what took too long, which interview questions flagged noise).
- TODO: baseline a quick team survey for week 6 pulse.
